messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Answer**

The total entropy change for a 1 kg ice block that is heated from 0 °C to 100 °C (at 1 atm) is

\[
\boxed{\Delta S \;\approx\; 2.53\times10^{3}\ \text{J K}^{-1}}
\]

---

### How it’s calculated

| Step | Process | ΔS (J K⁻¹) |
|------|---------|------------|
| 1 | Melting of ice at 0 °C (273.15 K) | \( \displaystyle \frac{L_f}{T_m}= \frac{333.55\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}}{273.15\ \text{K}} \approx 1.221\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}=1221\ \text{J K}^{-1}\) |
| 2 | Heating liquid water from 0 °C to 100 °C | \( \displaystyle \int_{273.15}^{373.15}\frac{C_p}{T}\,dT = C_p\,\ln\!\left(\frac{373.15}{273.15}\right)\)  
\(C_p\approx 4.18\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\) → \(4.18\ln(1.366)\approx1.305\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}=1305\ \text{J K}^{-1}\) |

Adding the two contributions:

\[
\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 1221\ \text{J K}^{-1} + 1305\ \text{J K}^{-1}
= 2526\ \text{J K}^{-1}\;\approx\;2.53\times10^{3}\ \text{J K}^{-1}.
\]

---

### Note on vaporisation

If the process were continued until the water fully vaporised at 100 °C (i.e., the final state were steam), an additional entropy increase of

\[
\Delta S_{\text{vap}} = \frac{L_v}{T_b} = \frac{2257\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}}{373.15\ \text{K}} \approx 6.05\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}=6050\ \text{J K}^{-1}
\]

would be added, giving a total of about \(8.58\times10^{3}\ \text{J K}^{-1}\).  
The value above (≈ 2.53 kJ K⁻¹) assumes the final state is liquid water at 100 °C.
